goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError on feeds whose items carry only description/summary, aborting the poll on every run so the feed is permanently never imported.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — raw_html cook_method stores remote article HTML verbatim as `cooked` with no sanitizer, so a `<script>` in any imported feed item executes on the forum origin for every viewer

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `raw_html` cook method that bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline: `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from remote/feed content with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), where `contents` comes from RSS (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) or remote fetch. There is no sanitizer applied in this path, and the embed view renders with `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), meaning any `<script>` or event-handler HTML from a feed item could execute in viewers’ browsers under the forum origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — the only gate on this unauthenticated GET endpoint is the client-supplied Referer header, so anyone with curl can drive server-side fetches and auto-create forum topics at will

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access control is based on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (and presence of the setting). This endpoint (`GET /embed/best`) is otherwise unauthenticated in the diff (no login requirement), and when no existing embed is found it enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` with the client-supplied `embed_url`, which can lead to server-side fetching via `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (`open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) and topic/post creation as `embed_by_username`. Since `Referer` is client-controlled/spoofable (e.g., curl can set it), the finding that the only gate is a client-supplied header enabling drive-by fetch/topic creation is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — CGI.unescapeHTML re-decodes text the feed already escaped, turning a feed author's `<script>` into live markup before it is stored as unsanitized HTML

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the feed item body is explicitly entity-decoded via `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then imported with `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a Post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `:raw_html`, skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This combination means an escaped payload like `<script>...` from the feed will be turned into live `<script>` markup and persisted/rendered unsanitized, enabling XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — the throttle key is the full embed_url, so `?a=1`, `?a=2`, ... each get a fresh 60s bucket and the rate limit plus the duplicate-topic guard are both trivially bypassed

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? uses `retrieved_key = "retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`, so changing only the querystring (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, etc.) produces different Redis keys and defeats the intended 60s throttle. Separately, perform_retrieve’s duplicate guard checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so the same underlying page with different query parameters is treated as a different embed_url and can trigger multiple imports/topics. Both behaviors are directly shown in the diff and allow trivial bypass of throttling/duplication prevention.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx and expire are not atomic, so a crash or redis hiccup between them leaves the throttle key with no TTL and that embed_url can never be retrieved again

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses two separate Redis commands: `setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or loses Redis connectivity after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key can remain without a TTL, causing `setnx` to fail forever for that embed_url and `retrieved_recently?` to always return true (permanent throttling). This defect is visible directly in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — every cache miss synchronously runs a full feed poll inside the job, so anonymous /embed/best requests can force repeated feed downloads and bulk imports

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when no `TopicEmbed` exists it unconditionally runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` if `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `PollFeed#poll_feed` performs a network fetch (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates/imports all items each time. Since `/embed/best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` on a miss (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), repeated anonymous embed misses (throttled only per-embed_url for 60s) can cause repeated full feed downloads and repeated bulk import attempts, which is unintended and can be abused for resource exhaustion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — staff skip the throttle entirely, so two concurrent requests both perform_retrieve, both create a topic, and the loser's TopicEmbed.create! raises RecordNotUnique on the unique index

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`, staff users pass `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever` (new file `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`). In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, `@opts[:no_throttle]` returns `false` immediately, bypassing the Redis `setnx` throttle/lock (`lib/topic_retriever.rb`). That means concurrent staff-triggered retrieves for the same `embed_url` can both enter `perform_retrieve`, both see `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` as false, and then both call `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `TopicEmbed.import`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when `embed.blank?`, it does `TopicEmbed.create!` with a unique index on `embed_url` (`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`). The loser will raise `RecordNotUnique` on that unique index (no rescue shown), causing job failure and potentially leaving inconsistent side effects (at minimum an exception path).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read has no size or time cap and pulls the whole remote body into the worker, so a slow or huge attacker-chosen response parks or OOMs a Sidekiq worker

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`, which fetches the entire remote response body into memory with no explicit timeout or size cap. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:36 — the success assertions live in an `after` hook, so they run outside the example body and silently apply to every current and future example in the context

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — "ALLOWALL" is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive and the spec asserts only the literal string, so the test stays green regardless of real browser framing behaviour

adjudication.rationale: The controller explicitly sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). `ALLOWALL` is not a standard/valid X-Frame-Options directive (standard values are e.g. `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, historically `ALLOW-FROM`), so browsers may ignore it or behave inconsistently, affecting real framing behavior. The spec only asserts the literal string `"ALLOWALL"`, so it would pass even if the value is ineffective for actual browser embedding.

Since `PostCreator` only sets `post.created_at` when `@opts[:created_at]` is present (see `lib/post_creator.rb` change area), the imported topic/post will now default to the import time rather than the original Disqus thread timestamp.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — the `-c/--category` method_option was removed, so any existing `disqus import ... -c Category` invocation now aborts with a Thor unknown-switch error and imports can no longer be targeted at a category

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and also deletes the logic that read `options[:category]` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — import_remote performs an unrescued live `open(url).read` per thread, so one dead/redirecting Disqus link raises OpenURI::HTTPError and aborts the whole import midway (previously the importer needed no network)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` instead of creating a local post. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`) with no rescue around network/HTTP failures. If any Disqus thread link is dead, redirects oddly, or returns non-2xx, `open-uri` can raise (e.g., `OpenURI::HTTPError`) and abort the import loop mid-run. This is a behavior change from the previous no-network importer and is a real reliability defect exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — return-value contract changed: PostCreator#create always made a new post, while import_remote returns nil for non-http links and returns the pre-existing post when the embed row already exists, so re-running the importer appends duplicate replies to an existing topic

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the importer now does `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` and then, if `post.present?`, iterates `t[:posts]` to add replies. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` delegates to `TopicEmbed.import`, which (a) returns `nil` for non-http(s) URLs (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`) and (b) returns the existing first post when a `TopicEmbed` row for the URL already exists (via `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `post = embed.post`). Because `topic_embeds.embed_url` is unique, re-running the Disqus importer for the same thread link will reuse the existing topic/post and append the replies again, creating duplicate replies in that existing topic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 — comments.appendChild` is called without checking that `#discourse-comments` exists, so a host page that loads the script before/without that element gets an uncaught TypeError and no embed

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `Jobs::PollFeed` job, the feed is fetched via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). This uses `open-uri` without specifying `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` or any size limit, so a slow/hanging server or extremely large response can block the scheduled Sidekiq worker indefinitely and/or cause excessive memory use during parsing. This reliability/performance failure is introduced by the diff and is directly grounded in the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote does open(url).read of an arbitrary remote page and runs Readability/Nokogiri over the whole body with no size cap or timeout, on a path reachable from public embed requests

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `open(url).read` (via `open-uri`) with no explicit timeouts or response size limits, then parses the full body through Readability/Nokogiri (`Readability::Document.new(...)`). This is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which is reachable from the public `GET /embed/best` path when no embed exists (`EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#retrieve` -> `fetch_http` -> `import_remote`). Although host is constrained to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, the lack of timeout/size cap still enables hanging/large-response DoS against the server.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 — post.user and post.url are dereferenced per post in the render loop with no preloading, adding roughly two extra queries per post on this public embed hot path

adjudication.rationale: The view loop in app/views/embed/best.html.erb does dereference post.user and post.url, but the diff does not show how @topic_view.posts is loaded (TopicView is not modified here). TopicView may already eager-load users (and post.url may not hit the DB), so the claim that there is "no preloading" and that it adds "roughly two extra queries per post" cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key is computed but never used, so there is no last-modified/conditional GET and every poll re-downloads and re-hashes the entire feed

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the `feed_key` method is defined (computes a Redis key from the feed URL) but is never referenced anywhere in the class. The actual polling path (`poll_feed`) always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of `feed_key` or any cached last-modified/etag value, so each run re-fetches the full feed. This is a concrete inefficiency/unfinished optimization rather than a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(feed_polling_url) and SimpleRSS.parse are unrescued, so any SocketError, OpenURI::HTTPError, timeout or malformed feed kills the whole hourly poll.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is executed without any exception handling. `open-uri` and `SimpleRSS.parse` can raise (e.g., `SocketError`, `OpenURI::HTTPError`, timeouts, malformed XML), which would bubble up and abort the scheduled job run (and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means no automatic retry).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError on feeds whose items carry only description/summary, aborting the poll on every run so the feed is permanently never imported.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that calling `i.content.scrub` can fail when `i.content` is absent/nil in many feeds that only provide description/summary, causing a NoMethodError and breaking polling; the golden additionally suggests a fallback, which is implied by the candidate mentioning description/summary-only items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — A single bad item raises out of the each loop, so all remaining items are skipped and, with retry disabled, are only re-attempted an hour later against the same failing item.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job iterates `rss.items.each` and performs per-item operations that can raise (e.g., `i.content.scrub` if `i.content` is nil, `open(...)`, or `TopicEmbed.import(...)`), but there is no per-item rescue. Any exception will abort the whole job and skip remaining items. Since `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set, the failed run will not be retried and processing is effectively deferred until the next hourly run, potentially repeatedly failing on the same problematic item.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — sidekiq_options retry: false means a transient network blip silently drops that hour's poll entirely with no retry and no recovery path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds Jobs::PollFeed as a scheduled Sidekiq job and explicitly sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). Since `poll_feed` performs network I/O (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`), transient failures would not be retried by Sidekiq for that execution, potentially delaying imports until the next hourly run. However, this is a resiliency/operational concern rather than a strictly verifiable defect from the diff alone (the next recurrence provides some recovery).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open() uses open-uri defaults with no open/read timeout, so a slow or hanging feed host can pin a Sidekiq worker for a very long time.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the job does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` after `require 'open-uri'`, using open-uri with no explicit open_timeout/read_timeout. If the feed host is slow or hangs, this network call can block the scheduled Sidekiq worker thread for an unbounded time, causing availability issues. This behavior is directly introduced by the diff and is a real operational defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote's open(url).read has no rescue and no timeout, so a 404/500/DNS failure or slow embedded host kills the RetrieveTopic job or holds a worker indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code calls `open(url).read` (via `open-uri`) with no explicit timeouts and no exception handling (`OpenURI::HTTPError`, `SocketError`, `Timeout::Error`, etc.). This method is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and thus from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job. As written, network failures (404/500/DNS) will raise and fail the job, and slow/hung connections may tie up a Sidekiq worker because no open/read timeout options are provided in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:35 — If the embedded post was deleted (Trashable default scope) embed.post is nil and PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError, permanently breaking every later poll for that URL.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally `PostRevisor.new(post)` when content changed. If the associated post record is missing or filtered out by a default scope (e.g., soft-deleted), `embed.post` can be nil and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will raise, breaking subsequent imports/updates for that embed_url. There is no nil-guard or recovery in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:25 — TopicEmbed.create! can raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique against the unique embed_url index when two retrievals race, and the exception is unrescued.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the code does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). If two jobs/processes import the same URL concurrently, both can observe `embed.blank?` and then race on `create!`, causing `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` to be raised and unhandled in this method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — URI(url) in absolutize_urls raises URI::InvalidURIError for feed links containing spaces or other illegal characters that still pass the http regex guard, aborting the import.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the URL guard is only `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which will still accept malformed URLs like ones containing spaces/illegal characters after the scheme. That URL is then passed into `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, which calls `uri = URI(url)` without rescuing `URI::InvalidURIError`. This would raise and abort the import transaction for such feed links, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx followed by a separate expire is non-atomic; a crash or exception between the two leaves a TTL-less redis key that blocks retrieval of that embed_url forever.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or raises between these calls, the key can be created without a TTL, causing `setnx` to fail forever on subsequent attempts and thus permanently treating the URL as "retrieved recently" (blocking retrieval indefinitely). This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — perform_retrieve runs the entire feed poll inline and unrescued, so any feed-level error propagates and the fetch_http fallback never runs.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, when SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline and does not rescue any exceptions. Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `SimpleRSS.parse` with no error handling, so any network/parse error will propagate and abort `perform_retrieve` before reaching `fetch_http`, preventing the HTTP fallback path from running.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — The exists? check and the subsequent import are not atomic, so concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs (staff bypass the throttle) can both import the same embed_url.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, the flow is `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and then later `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)`. That check+act is not atomic, so concurrent RetrieveTopic runs (especially with `no_throttle` for staff) can both pass the `exists?` check and then race in TopicEmbed.import. TopicEmbed.import does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, attempts `TopicEmbed.create!` while a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` was added in the diff. The loser of the race will hit a unique-constraint exception (not rescued), causing job failure and potentially extra work/side effects before rollback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds with no attempt cap or failure state, so a permanently unretrievable URL loops forever.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the script unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` after 30 seconds with no max attempts or error/failure UI. Given `EmbedController#best` renders `loading` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil (and only enqueues retrieval), an embed URL that never successfully imports will keep the iframe/page reloading indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every request enqueues another RetrieveTopic job with no dedup, so the 30s reload loop plus Sidekiq's default retries floods the queue with jobs that keep refetching a failing URL.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no embed exists it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The `loading.html.erb` template reloads the page every 30s, so repeated client reloads will enqueue additional `RetrieveTopic` jobs with no enqueue-side dedup/throttling. `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` does not set `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so exceptions from `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`open(url)` can trigger Sidekiq retries. While `TopicRetriever` has a 60s Redis throttle that can make extra jobs no-op, the diff still shows a realistic queue-growth/perf risk from repeated enqueues rather than a direct correctness failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — If the topic is deleted while the topic_embeds row remains, TopicView.new raises NotFound and the embed stays broken because perform_retrieve bails whenever the embed row exists.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, if `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns a `topic_id`, it unconditionally calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` without checking the topic still exists. Separately, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` immediately returns if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so a stale `topic_embeds` row (e.g., topic deleted but embed row remains; no dependent cleanup is shown in this diff) would both (a) likely cause `TopicView.new` to fail and (b) prevent re-retrieval/recreation because retrieval bails whenever the embed row exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute is also applied to the loading render, so a shared cache can serve the stale loading page after retrieval succeeds.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after the `if topic_id ... else render 'loading' end` branch. That means the `loading` response also gets the same cache headers/TTL as the successful response, so an intermediary/shared cache could continue serving the cached loading page for up to 1 minute even after the topic has been retrieved and would otherwise render highlights.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — cook() returns the raw attribute verbatim for raw_html posts, so untrusted remote HTML is stored in `cooked` (post.rb:321) with no sanitizing pipeline, yielding stored XSS wherever cooked is rendered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `Post.cook_methods` with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` and `import_remote` ingest remote HTML (RSS `i.content` / Readability `doc.content`) and create posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This makes untrusted remote HTML effectively stored/displayed without sanitization, creating a stored-XSS risk wherever `cooked` is rendered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 — RSS/Atom item content is passed to TopicEmbed.import with no sanitization at all (and CGI.unescapeHTML first re-activates entity-encoded markup), so any script/iframe/event-handler in the feed becomes a raw_html post.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the feed item body is taken as `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passed directly to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`. The embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore any HTML (including `<script>`, iframes, or event-handler attributes) present in the feed content will be stored and rendered without sanitization, and `CGI.unescapeHTML` can convert entity-encoded markup back into active tags.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — raw post.cooked` renders post HTML unescaped on a Discourse-origin page that is deliberately framed by third parties; cooked is no longer guaranteed sanitized for raw_html posts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_method == :raw_html` which makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly (app/models/post.rb), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and the spec asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`, confirming cooked can contain arbitrary HTML. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), which will output that HTML unescaped inside a Discourse-origin iframe, creating an XSS risk if imported/feed content contains unsafe markup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — The imported URL is interpolated into `<a href='#{url}'>` without HTML escaping, so a feed item link (only checked with /^https?:\/\//) can inject attributes or markup into the stored post.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `url` is only checked with `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` and then interpolated into HTML as `"#{url}"` (no escaping). A crafted URL like `http://x.com' onclick='...` would pass the regex and inject attributes/markup into the stored post. This is amplified because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so the injected HTML would execute.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url)` (open-uri) fetches an attacker-supplied embed_url server side: it follows redirects and allows arbitrary ports, so an open redirect or a port on the embeddable host reaches internal/metadata services (SSRF).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the code does `open(url).read` on the supplied `url` (diff shows `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`). That `url` can originate from the `embed_url` request parameter (`EmbedController#best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` with `embed_url`, which flows through `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). While `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, it does not restrict scheme/port and does not prevent following redirects. Since `open-uri` follows redirects by default, an attacker-controlled URL on the allowed host can redirect the server-side request to other hosts/internal services (SSRF), and arbitrary ports are also allowed because only the host is checked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` passes an unvalidated setting to Kernel#open, which treats a leading "|" as a shell command and permits file:// URLs, turning a site-setting write into command execution/file read.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `open` (with `require 'open-uri'`) on a site setting without validation. With Ruby's Kernel#open behavior, a value starting with `|` can be treated as a pipe to a shell command, and `open-uri` also enables non-HTTP schemes (e.g., `file://`) depending on Ruby/version/config, turning a setting change into potential command execution or local file read. The diff introduces the setting (`feed_polling_url`) and this unsafe usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Access control for this public endpoint rests solely on the Referer header matching one host (no scheme check, trivially forged by non-browser clients), so the embed page and its side effects are reachable by anyone.

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` gates access only by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and then allows framing (`X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`). The Referer header is not a trustworthy authentication mechanism (can be omitted or trivially forged by non-browser clients) and there’s no scheme/cryptographic validation. Because `best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` when no embed exists, a forged Referer can trigger retrieval/import side effects without actually being embedded by the allowed site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — An unauthenticated request can enqueue RetrieveTopic for any URL, causing a server-side fetch and automatic topic/post creation as the embed_by_username user; the redis throttle is per-URL so distinct URLs are unlimited.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, any request that passes `ensure_embeddable` (based solely on `request.referer` host) will enqueue `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` whenever no existing `TopicEmbed` is found, without validating `params[:embed_url]` itself or applying rate limiting at the controller level. The job calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which can result in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` doing a server-side `open(url)` and creating/updating a topic/post as `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` (`TopicRetriever#fetch_http`). The redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed by the full URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so an attacker can bypass it by varying URLs/paths, enabling unbounded fetches/auto-topic creation (at least for URLs on `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, since `invalid_host?` blocks other hosts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — X-Frame-Options is set to the non-standard value "ALLOWALL", which browsers ignore, removing framing protection for every origin rather than just the embeddable host (clickjacking).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does set `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, and "ALLOWALL" is not a standard X-Frame-Options directive (so browser handling is inconsistent / often treated as invalid). However, the controller also enforces embedding restrictions server-side by requiring `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, so it’s not simply “framing allowed for every origin” as the finding claims. This is still a concrete security/robustness concern (nonstandard header + relying on Referer rather than a standard `frame-ancestors` policy), but not a clearly verifiable defect exactly as stated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`), so any origin that is a prefix/substring of the forum URL (e.g. https://forum.example.co) is accepted.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This accepts any `e.origin` that is a substring/prefix of `discourseUrl` (e.g., `https://forum.example.co` will match `https://forum.example.com/...` at index 0), so an attacker-controlled origin that is a prefix could bypass the check and send `discourse-resize` messages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage targetOrigin is the reflected full Referer URL instead of a fixed origin, making the destination of the message attacker-influenced rather than pinned.
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that `postMessage` is using the full reflected Referer URL as `targetOrigin` rather than a proper origin (scheme+host+port). The candidate emphasizes the attacker-influenced aspect, but it’s the same root issue of not pinning to an origin (which also leads to dropped messages).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — The new skip_validations option lets callers persist posts bypassing all ActiveRecord validations (spam/host/content checks) on content that originates from attacker-triggered imports.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` in `lib/post_revisor.rb`, enabling callers to persist edited posts without any ActiveRecord validations. This new option is actually used by newly-added attacker-influenced import paths: `TopicEmbed.import` updates an existing post via `PostRevisor#revise!(..., skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)` and also creates posts via `PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true` plus `cook_method: :raw_html` (which returns `raw` directly in `Post#cook`). Since `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` can be enqueued from `EmbedController#best` based on request params and the system fetches remote content (`open(url).read` / RSS), this change concretely allows imported/updated content to bypass validations, making the finding accurate and security-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 — Spec mocks TopicRetriever.new/retrieve but EmbedController#best calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic) instead, so it only passes via inline job execution and never asserts the enqueue, its user_id/embed_url args, or the 'loading' render

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `'loading'`; it does not call `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` in the “no previous embed” case, and does not assert the job enqueue (including args) or the `'loading'` render. This is a real, diff-grounded test mismatch/coverage gap, but the claim that it "only passes via inline job execution" cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:50 — TopicView.expects(:new) returns nil so @topic_view is nil and the embed/best view is never exercised; the test verifies only the mock call

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the example "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" sets `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` but does not stub a return value, so Mocha will return `nil` by default and `@topic_view` will be nil in the controller (`@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)`). The spec also does not use `render_views`, so it only verifies the constructor call and does not exercise the `embed/best` template which expects `@topic_view.posts`/`@topic_view.topic`. This is a concrete test-quality gap created by the mocking, not a production defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:10 — response.should_not be_success` passes for any non-2xx, including a 500 from an unrelated crash; no status code or exception type is asserted (same at lines 16 and 26)

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the assertions `response.should_not be_success` (e.g., in "is 404 without an embed_url" and other error-path tests) only verify the response is not 2xx, so they would still pass on a 500 caused by an unrelated crash. The diff shows no explicit status-code checks (e.g., 404/403) or exception assertions for those cases, making the new tests overly weak/ambiguous rather than validating the intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — "is 404 without an embed_url" never reaches params.require: embeddable_host defaults to '' so ensure_embeddable raises InvalidAccess first, and the test would pass with the missing-param check deleted

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `best`, so `params.require(:embed_url)` is not reached if `ensure_embeddable` raises first. `ensure_embeddable` raises when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` (and the default in `site_settings.yml` is `''`, i.e., blank). Therefore the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do; get :best; response.should_not be_success; end` will fail (non-success) due to the filter, even if the missing `embed_url` check were removed. This is a real, diff-grounded test-quality issue rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:35 — Success/X-Frame-Options assertions live in an `after` hook rather than in the examples, so they run after mocha verification and are not attributable to a specific example

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb within the `context "success"`, there is an `after do` block (around lines 34-39) asserting `response.should be_success` and `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'].should == "ALLOWALL"`. This makes those expectations run after every example in that context rather than being stated in the individual `it` blocks, which can make failures less clearly attributable to a specific example and can interact poorly with mock verification ordering (mocha is used via `expects`/`stubs` in the same context). This is a test-structure issue, not a runtime defect in the app code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — "requires feed_polling_url" is vacuous: feed_polling_enabled defaults to false so execute short-circuits on the first condition and the test passes even if the feed_polling_url guard were removed

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed is only called if feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the "requires feed_polling_url" example only stubs SiteSetting.feed_polling_url to nil and does not stub feed_polling_enabled?. The diff also sets feed_polling_enabled default to false in config/site_settings.yml, so execute will short-circuit on the first condition and never evaluate the URL guard, making the test pass even if the feed_polling_url check were removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:24 — "requires embed_by_username" is vacuous for the same reason: the default-false feed_polling_enabled guard short-circuits before embed_by_username is ever consulted

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed is only called if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the test `it "requires embed_by_username"` only stubs `embed_by_username` to nil and does not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true nor provide a non-blank `feed_polling_url`. Given site_settings.yml sets feed_polling_enabled default to false, the guard will short-circuit on `feed_polling_enabled?` and never consult `embed_by_username`, making the test vacuous as the finding claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — absolutize_urls edge cases are untested; a protocol-relative href like //cdn.host/x matches start_with?('/') and is rewritten to prefix + /cdn.host/x, and document-relative "images/x" is left untouched

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the condition `href.start_with?('/')` will also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.host/x`. The rewrite `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"` would turn that into something like `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.host/x`, which is incorrect and breaks the intended external asset URL. This behavior is directly implied by the added code. The method also only rewrites root-relative paths and leaves other relative forms (e.g., `images/x`) untouched, which may be an incompleteness, but the protocol-relative rewrite is a concrete correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:39 — The update test asserts only that cooked changed; it does not assert content_sha1 was updated, that no duplicate topic/TopicEmbed row was created, or that identical content skips the revision

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb the "Supports updating the post" example only asserts `post.cooked` matches the new contents. The implementation in TopicEmbed.import has nontrivial branching: it reuses an existing TopicEmbed (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`), conditionally revises the post only when `content_sha1` changes, and updates `embed.content_sha1` via `update_column`. The spec does not verify that the existing TopicEmbed row is reused (no duplicate), that `content_sha1` is updated on change, or that identical content skips revision.
